text:
ConocoPhillips inched down 0.14% today to $142.14, essentially flat despite oil prices remaining elevated. The tiny decline came as crude markets digested mixed signals: while Middle East tensions continued—Iran escalated attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi Aramco facilities came under fire—U.S. oil prices actually eased slightly to $96.24 per barrel as traders processed the latest International Energy Agency report on global supply.

The stock's real momentum remains the 11.86% gain over the past two weeks, which tracks with the broader oil market's climb driven by geopolitical supply concerns. The gap between U.S. crude ($96) and global oil ($125 per barrel) is wide, reflecting how Middle East tensions are rippling through energy markets unevenly—benefiting oil producers overall, but today's pause suggests investors are waiting to see whether the shipping attacks will actually tighten supplies enough to sustain higher prices.
